title: Composition-compatible open restriction for maps identical over an open
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible commutative condensed coefficient ring of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For every scheme $T$ put $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$, where $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ is the pulled-back ring and the category is the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Use the module direct images and inverse images of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], with the coefficient identifications induced by composition of pullbacks from the point and the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ and $j':U\hookrightarrow Z'$ be quasi-compact open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $h:Z'\to Z$ satisfy $hj'=j$ and $h^{-1}(j(U))=j'(U)$ as open subschemes. There is a canonical natural isomorphism $r_h:j^*Rh_*\xrightarrow{\sim}j'^*$: on a K-injective representative $I$, at $V\to U$, its underived map is the identity on $I(V)$ under $V\times_Z Z'\cong V$. Module actions use the canonical pulled-back coefficient identifications. For $j'':U\hookrightarrow Z''$ and $k:Z''\to Z'$ satisfying the same two conditions, with the compositor $\kappa$ of [lem-sfb-module-derived-compositor-coherence],
$$r_{hk}=(r_k)\circ(r_h Rk_*)\circ(j^*\kappa_{h,k}).$$
For $h=1_Z$, $r_h$ is the identity after the canonical direct-image identity comparison. Properness, scheme-theoretic density, and a field of definition are not assumed.

source.place: Refinement isomorphisms and Independence: restriction of composites to X (returned proof step 3)

proof.text: Work on the small sites fixed in the statement. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization](1), the sites of $U$ identify with the slices at $j$ and $j'$. Here only the site equivalence is used, not the constant-coefficient assertion (2). By [lem-sfb-coefficient-sections-localization], applied to the objects $j:U\to Z$ of $Z_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ and $j':U\to Z'$ of $Z'_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, the abelian inverse images $j^*_{\mathrm{Ab}}$, $j'^*_{\mathrm{Ab}}$ are restriction to these localized sites, and the coefficient maps $\alpha_j:j^*_{\mathrm{Ab}}\Lambda_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_U$, $\alpha_{j'}$ are isomorphisms; that node holds for every commutative condensed ring, so it covers all admissible $\Lambda$ of [sk-def-localizing-closure], including $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with its $\ell$-adic topology. Under [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], restriction evaluates a module on $V\to U$ by evaluating the original module on the composite $V\to T$. Since $\alpha_j$ is invertible, the extension of scalars in $j^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_j}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(j^*_{\mathrm{Ab}})$ [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] is canonically the identity on underlying sheaves, with $\Lambda_U$ acting through $\alpha_j^{-1}$. Thus $j^*$ and $j'^*$ are precisely these restriction functors with those coefficient identifications. By [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport], the internal module categories and their specified pullbacks and pushforwards identify by additive exact equivalences with sectionwise modules over the reconstructed coefficient ring sheaves $B_T$. Such an equivalence identifies complexes, acyclic complexes and homotopy classes, hence preserves and reflects K-injectivity. Finally [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main] gives that the module pullback $f^*$ is additive and exact for every morphism of schemes $f$ and every commutative condensed ring; in particular $j^*$, $j'^*$ and every $k^*$ below are exact.

source.place: Tag 03CE, lemma-localize-given-products; localized module restrictions with the cited coefficient-section localization and module-pullback exactness

proof.text: For $v:V\to U$, the projection $V\times_Z Z'\to V$ is an isomorphism with inverse $(1_V,j'v)$. Indeed the other projection factors through $h^{-1}(j(U))=j'(U)$; under that open-subscheme identification its map to $U$ equals $v$ after projection, since $hj'=j$ and the open immersion $j$ is a monomorphism. These two maps are inverse by the fibre-product universal property. They commute with every arrow $V_1\to V_2$ over $U$. By [def-sfb-finite-lower-star], $(h_*M)(V\to Z)=M(V\times_Z Z')$. Therefore step 1 gives a natural underived isomorphism $c_h:j^*h_*\xrightarrow{\sim}j'^*$, identity on $M(V)$ after this fibre-product identification. Its coefficient action is the same on both sides: in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] the direct image action uses the adjunct structural map, and restriction identifies this map with the identity coefficient map on $U$ for the localized identity morphism. The pullbacks from the point are identified by the composition identifications stipulated in the statement. Consequently the section identity is linear, commutes with restrictions and all module morphisms, and defines $c_h$ and its inverse.

source.place: Tag 0D6G, lemma-restrict-direct-image-open: underived restriction identity, specialized to the identity localized map

proof.text: By [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], every complex of sectionwise $B_T$-modules on our small site has a K-injective resolution. The exact equivalences in step 1 transport these to internal modules. For $K\in D_{Z'}$, choose a K-injective $I$ and $a:K\xrightarrow{\sim}QI$, where $Q$ denotes localization. By [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], $Rh_*K$ is represented by $h_*I$. Exactness of $j^*$ and $j'^*$ from step 1 means that they act termwise on all complexes and preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Hence, under the canonical identifications $j^*Rh_*K\cong Q(j^*h_*I)$ and $j'^*K\cong Q(j'^*I)$ (the latter induced by $a$), define $r_{h,K}$ by $Q(c_{h,I})$. It is an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], each derived morphism between K-injective representatives is represented by a unique homotopy class of chain maps. The degreewise naturality of $c_h$ therefore proves naturality of $r_h$. Changing $I$ or $a$ uses the unique corresponding homotopy class between K-injectives; the same naturality square shows that the resulting $r_{h,K}$ agrees. This proves the stated canonical normalization and independence of resolutions.

source.place: Tag 0D6G, lemma-restrict-direct-image-open, K-injective computation; existence from Tag 079P, injectives-theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck, and independence from Tag 070I, derived-lemma-K-injective

proof.text: To compare successive maps, take a K-injective complex $I$ on $Z''$. The adjunction $k^*\dashv k_*$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] has additive left adjoint $k^*$, exact by [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main] (step 1). Thus [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], with $v=k^*$ and $u=k_*$, makes $k_*I$ K-injective on $Z'$. We can compute $Rk_*$ on $I$, and then $Rh_*$ on the already K-injective $k_*I$, with no intermediate replacement. The same argument applies to $h_*k_*I$. This checks the preservation hypothesis required for computing all the comparisons below on this one representative.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives; exact module inverse image supplies its left-adjoint hypothesis

proof.text:
The composite $hk$ satisfies $(hk)j''=j$ and $(hk)^{-1}(j(U))=k^{-1}(j'(U))=j''(U)$, so steps 2–3 also define $r_{hk}$. By [lem-sfb-module-derived-compositor-coherence], on the representatives of step 4 the map $\kappa_{h,k}$ is the inverse of the termwise module compositor. At $V\to U$ its underlying map is induced by the canonical identification
$$(V\times_Z Z')\times_{Z'}Z''\cong V\times_Z Z''.$$
The identification of step 2 for $h$ is the projection to $V$ with inverse $(1_V,j'v)$; the identification for $k$ has inverse $(1_V,j''v)$. Their composite, after the displayed associator, is exactly the inverse $(1_V,j''v)$ for $hk$: both have the same projection to $V$ and the same projection $j''v$ to $Z''$, so the fibre-product universal property makes them equal. Evaluating the two composites on $I$ therefore gives the same map $I(V)\to I(V)$, namely the identity. All maps are module maps by step 2 and the cited module compositor. Thus already as maps of complexes,
$$c_{hk,I}=c_{k,I}\circ c_{h,k_*I}\circ (j^*\kappa_{h,k})_I.$$
Localize this equality and use the canonical representative identifications from steps 3–4. This gives exactly $r_{hk}=r_k\circ(r_hRk_*)\circ(j^*\kappa_{h,k})$. It holds for every $K\cong QI$ and is an equality of natural transformations by step 3.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, together with Tag 0D6G, lemma-restrict-direct-image-open; explicit fibre-product computation of their coherence

proof.text: For $h=1_Z$ the condition $hj'=j$ identifies $j'$ with $j$, and the projection $V\times_Z Z\to V$ and its inverse $(1_V,jv)$ are the usual identity base-change maps. Hence $c_{1_Z}$ is the sectionwise identity after the underived identity-direct-image comparison. By [lem-sfb-module-derived-compositor-coherence], the canonical derived identity comparison is precisely the one induced by that sectionwise identity. On every K-injective representative $r_{1_Z}$ is therefore the identity after that comparison, and step 3 gives the claimed natural identity. None of the constructions used properness, density or a field of definition.

tool_uses.why: Its site equivalence identifies the open pro-etale sites with slices; this generic localization tool does not impose constant coefficients.
Its exact equivalences and comparisons allow sectionwise ringed-module computation for internal condensed modules, preserving the actual module operations.
Supplies unbounded K-injective resolutions on small ringed sites; the exact internal/sectionwise equivalence transports them to our categories.
Specifies the ordinary unbounded total module direct image computed on K-injectives, without a bounded or completed substitute.
The generic additive exact-left-adjoint theorem permits computing Rk_* and then Rh_* using I and k_*I without an intervening resolution.

States that abelian inverse image along an object V->B of B_proet is restriction to the localized site, with invertible alpha, for every commutative condensed ring; replaces sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients, whose Qbar_l is the finite-subextension ring and so does not cover the l-adic-topology Qbar_l of sk-def-localizing-closure.
Exactness of module pullback for every morphism of schemes and every commutative condensed ring (needed for j^*, j'^* and the exact left adjoint k^* of step 4); no node of the unit gives it.
